bill.title: Calling upon local communities to support organizations that provide resources and aid Gold Shield Families in their time of need.
bill.latestActionText: Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
bill.officialSummary: This resolution encourages local communities throughout the United States to support nonprofit organizations that provide resources to Gold Shield Families during their time of need. Gold Shield Families consist of the families of fallen police officers, firefighters, emergency medical technicians, correction officers, emergency dispatch officers, and emergency service providers.

classification.plainSummary: This resolution encourages local communities across the United States to support nonprofit organizations that help families of fallen first responders. These families—referred to as Gold Shield Families—include those who have lost police officers, firefighters, paramedics, corrections officers, dispatchers, and other emergency personnel. The resolution is a non-binding expression of support and does not create new programs or impose requirements.

plain.whatItDoes: This resolution would encourage local communities throughout the United States to support nonprofit organizations that provide resources to Gold Shield Families during their time of need.
plain.whoItTouches: People living where a disaster hits.
plain.everydayEffect: If it passed, the change would show up in what help arrives, and when. Nothing has changed yet. This kind of resolution does not become law, even if it passes.
plain.source: Reworded from the official summary. Staff at the Congressional Research Service wrote that summary. It is public domain, and the full text of it is further down this page.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
